marketUnits2020UpperBound.note: e2W sales were below this annual threshold

countries.name: Kenya

tam.whyRange: Low is the 2024 registration count; base is 25,277 e-units ÷ an estimated 15% e-share (~168,500, rounded); high is trade-data consumption. These use different market definitions.

countries.policy: Finance Act 2026 retains zero-rating for electric motorcycles and Li-ion batteries; local-content provisions in the National e-Mobility Policy. Spiro reports over 15,000 Kenyan bikes, about 60% of the measured e2W market.

countries.name: Uganda

tam.whyRange: Base is inferred from 30,000+ e2W at roughly one fifth of motorcycle sales; the high estimate uses trade data.

countries.policy: Established e-motorcycle activity; 134 swap stations serve roughly 950 compatible vehicles.

countries.name: Rwanda

tam.whyRange: No comparable market-size data found; validate registration and fleet data before sizing.

countries.policy: Foreign electric two-wheelers reportedly exempt from import taxes; more than 100 swap stations serve about 4,000 compatible vehicles.

countries.name: Tanzania

tam.whyRange: Imports are used as a market proxy; registrations and domestic production should be verified.

countries.policy: Regional expansion candidate; current country-specific e2W policy and import duty need verification.

countries.name: Nigeria

tam.whyRange: Imports, an estimated total market, and trade-data consumption are not directly comparable; low/high span the reported values.

countries.policy: EV import duty reportedly cut to zero and VAT exempt; secondary-source claims need confirmation with Nigeria Customs. Lagos okada restrictions constrain use cases.

countries.name: Ethiopia

tam.whyRange: No reliable two-wheeler unit sales dataset identified.

countries.policy: Fossil-fuel vehicle import ban and later ICE kit restrictions are reported; Addis stopped issuing two-wheeler licences in 2019. Gig-fleet potential is a founder estimate of 150,000–200,000 units over 10–15 years.

countries.name: Ghana

tam.whyRange: 2024 imports used as a proxy, not an independently verified annual sales figure.

countries.policy: No country-specific e2W policy, duty, or registration series included in this sizing.

countries.name: Morocco

tam.whyRange: Available e-moped import values do not establish total two-wheeler market size.

averageImportPriceUSD.formula: H1 import value ÷ H1 imported units.

countries.policy: Low unit import values point to a material mismatch against a premium scooter price; annualized imports are an assumption.

countries.name: South Africa

tam.whyRange: Available e-moped import values do not establish total two-wheeler market size.

averageImportPriceUSD.formula: H1 import value ÷ H1 imported units.

countries.policy: Imported e-unit value is low; Ather should validate premium willingness to pay and channel economics before entry.

countries.name: Egypt

tam.whyRange: No unit volume data identified; market size is not estimated.

countries.policy: Large Chinese e-scooter importer, but no unit data found; imports are described as low-cost consumer vehicles.

competitors.name: Spiro
competitors.note: 100,000+ bikes and 2,500+ stations reported; $100M funding in 2025, $50M in 2026 and $180M+ earlier; says petrol bikes are the real competitor.

competitors.name: Ampersand
competitors.note: Battery-swapping operator; swap networks are largely closed.

competitors.name: Roam
competitors.note: Reported retail price around KSh290,000, converted at the model exchange-rate assumption.

competitors.name: Yadea
competitors.note: Launched 5 models; top-end price reported at $3,000.

competitors.name: Bajaj / TVS / Honda
competitors.note: Bajaj is reported at about 36% of Nigeria unit sales; petrol bikes are the core competitive alternative.

pathA.name: A · Commercial-ready
pathA.challenge: Ather scooters are home-charged today; this path needs a swap-compatible variant or a network partner.

pathB.name: B · Premium consumer
pathB.challenge: Premium landed retail pricing is a model assumption; price gap is acute in low-cost import markets.

caveats: India ex-showroom price is used as an ex-factory proxy; this likely overstates export cost.
The current country-specific import duty and EAC remission eligibility need confirmation.
Container loading counts, assembly-line cost, and all-in logistics ranges are modelling assumptions.

riderEconomics.priceAssumption: Vehicle price uses Roam's reported retail anchor; actual purchase terms and financing are unverified.

supplyChain.status: User-supplied working hypothesis; not independently verified. Confirm process ownership, supplier geography, ERP / factory systems, routes and service-parts footprint with Ather before external or investment use.

flow.title: Tier-1 + global sourcing
flow.subtitle: India auto hubs · APAC cell / electronics suppliers
flow.details: Chassis, body, brakes, tyres and suspension; battery cells, electronics and motor materials.

flow.title: Hosur manufacturing
flow.subtitle: Battery packs · BMS · vehicle assembly
flow.details: Core electronics / pack assembly and vehicle manufacturing; validate plant-level process map.

flow.title: Quality + dispatch
flow.subtitle: Factory QA · export preparation
flow.details: Quality release, export configuration, spares allocation and shipment documentation.

flow.title: Ocean freight
flow.subtitle: India → Mombasa / Dar es Salaam
flow.details: Freight, customs clearance, port handling and inland delivery; lane transit is a separately sourced estimate.

flow.title: Country channel
flow.subtitle: Distributor · Experience Centre · dealer
flow.details: CBU pilot through local partner; service training, homologation, warranty and registration.

flow.title: Rider + lifecycle support
flow.subtitle: Vehicle · service parts · charging
flow.details: Customer delivery, regional service-parts availability, service centres and charging / swap-partner interfaces.

supportFlows.title: Supplier risk controls
supportFlows.details: Diversification, local backups and redesign options; verify supplier strategy and localization readiness.

supportFlows.title: Information systems
supportFlows.details: ERP / SAP, IoT and quality-gate visibility are proposed data integration points; verify actual platforms, access and event coverage.

supportFlows.title: Charging infrastructure
supportFlows.details: Ather Grid is a distinct infrastructure workstream; map equipment logistics and partner responsibilities for Africa.

supportFlows.title: Reverse logistics
supportFlows.details: Warranty returns, batteries, repair loops and end-of-life handling require country-specific process and compliance design.

supplyChain.africaAssemblyGate: Consider contract SKD / CKD assembly only after verified annual demand exceeds ~4–5k in one country or a confirmed policy requirement changes the economics.

roadmap.name: Prove the channel
roadmap.mode: Distributor-led CBU pilot · Kenya (Sri Lanka playbook)
roadmap.gate: Proceed only after duty, homologation, warranty and channel economics are confirmed.

roadmap.name: Expand selectively
roadmap.gate: Scale country by country against adoption, service and contribution-margin evidence.

roadmap.name: Localize by contract
roadmap.gate: One country exceeds ~4–5k annual units, or verified policy makes assembly necessary.

roadmap.name: Build only at scale
roadmap.mode: Own African plant · Path A + swap partner
roadmap.gate: Require durable demand, service economics and interoperable or partnered swap access.

risks.mitigation: Stress-test naira, birr and shilling exposure; use hard-currency budgets and refresh FX triggers before each order.
Model tax upside as optional; confirm Kenya Finance Act status and country tariff schedules.
Partner before committing to a commercial battery architecture; verify compatibility in writing.
Test lease / asset-finance partners and total cost of ownership with commercial riders.
Run a paid pilot; do not assume premium demand from broad e2W growth.
Reconcile registrations, imports and sales before scaling; keep country TAM ranges visible.
Refresh quotes and test landed-cost sensitivity before pilot purchase orders.

verificationItems: Import duty on e-motorcycles (HS 8711.60) and CKD kits, country by country.
Current USD/INR and a fresh India–East Africa container rate.
Kenyan and Nigerian registration data (KNBS/KRA, NBS); reported sources conflict.
Egypt, Rwanda and Ethiopia two-wheeler unit volumes.
Packing counts per container and assembly-line fixed-cost assumptions.
Nigeria duty and VAT status with Nigeria Customs; S20 is a secondary source.
Refresh S27 freight quote; source is undated.
Confirm current EAC CKD remission terms; S26 dates to 2020.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated Kenya export pilot. Do not approve African manufacturing yet.
recommendation.summary: Use export-led CBU entry to learn about premium willingness to pay, product-market fit, after-sales needs and channel economics. Treat East Africa as the near-term learning cluster; treat continental volume and assembly as conditional options.

gates.title: Market proof
gates.text: Named distributor, rider interviews and a paid pilot cohort; validate premium conversion against petrol alternatives.

gates.title: Unit economics
gates.text: Customs-confirmed duty, refreshed freight, warranty/service cost and positive contribution margin at realized price.

gates.title: Scale trigger
gates.text: Repeatable demand supports ≥4–5k annual units in one country before contract assembly is evaluated.

recommendation.decision: Leadership decision requested: authorize a time-boxed Kenya CBU pilot and diligence budget; defer assembly-capex approval.
